title: Mormon’s letter
summary: Mormon writes to his beloved son, saying he is still alive and will write of grievous matters.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon writes again to his son to tell him he is still alive and that he will write of grievous matters.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing a letter.
unspecified_visual_details: Writing materials, clothing, setting, and the son's presence are not specified.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the son receiving the letter; the verse does not say he is present.

title: Battle losses
summary: Mormon reports a severe battle with the Lamanites that his side did not win, the deaths of Archeantus, Luram, and Emron, and many other losses.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he had a severe battle with the Lamanites and did not conquer.
Archeantus, Luram, and Emron fell by the sword, and many choice men were lost.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A letter-writing image may carry the reported battle losses in narration rather than depicting a new battle.
unspecified_visual_details: The battle's location, participants beyond those named, and circumstances of the deaths are unspecified.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are events reported in the letter, not necessarily a present-time battle scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the named dead or the battle as present unless treating it as a clearly separate illustrative recollection.

title: Fear for the people
summary: Mormon fears the Lamanites will destroy the people. He says they do not repent, are stirred to anger, and react angrily or harden their hearts when he teaches.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon fears the Lamanites will destroy the people and says they do not repent.
Mormon says he labors with them continually; sharp speech makes them tremble and anger, while gentler speech is met with hardened hearts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing while his words describe his continuing labor among the people.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s specific appearance, location, and response in any particular teaching moment are unspecified.

narration.text: I am laboring with them continually

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The people's anger and hardening are reported, not a single specified event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular sermon, confrontation, or visible supernatural departure of the Spirit.

title: A call to keep laboring
summary: Mormon describes the people's loss of love and desire for blood and revenge, then urges his son that they continue their labor.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says the people have lost love for one another and continually thirst for blood and revenge.
Mormon urges his son that they labor diligently rather than cease, while in mortal life, to conquer the enemy of righteousness and rest in God's kingdom.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing the appeal in the letter.
unspecified_visual_details: The people are not tied to a specific visible incident in these verses.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: “Enemy of all righteousness” is figurative teaching, not a described visible being.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a literal enemy figure or a battle implied by the figurative phrase.

title: Prisoners at Sherrizah
summary: Mormon reports that the Lamanites hold men, women, and children taken from the tower of Sherrizah. He reports that the women's husbands and the children's fathers were slain, and describes the captives' deprivation.

explicit_facts.text: According to information Mormon received from Amoron, the Lamanites hold many men, women, and children taken from the tower of Sherrizah.
Mormon reports that the women's husbands and the children's fathers were slain, and that the captives are given only a little water.
Mormon reports that the women and children are fed the flesh of their slain family members.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The letter may be shown with an austere, non-graphic visual emphasis on captivity and deprivation.
unspecified_visual_details: The captives' exact number, appearance, and the place where they are held are unspecified.

narration.text: there were men, women, and children

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a reported atrocity, not a new present-tense event.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict gore, the slain bodies, or graphic consumption.

title: Moriantum’s atrocities reported
summary: Mormon compares the Lamanites' abomination with worse conduct by his own people in Moriantum, reporting the capture and abuse, torture, killing, and consumption of Lamanite daughters.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says his people in Moriantum committed an abomination exceeding that of the Lamanites, taking many Lamanite daughters prisoner and violating their chastity and virtue.
Mormon reports that his people tortured the captives to death and devoured their flesh, treating it as a token of bravery.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A non-graphic letter-writing image can carry the account without staging the violence.
unspecified_visual_details: The captives' identities, number beyond “many,” and the time and precise setting of the reported acts are unspecified.

narration.text: For behold, many of the daughters of the Lamanites have they taken prisoners

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage reports past atrocities; it does not provide a present-time scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage sexual violence, torture, graphic injury, or cannibalism.

title: Mormon laments the people
summary: Mormon laments how far the people have fallen from their former civility and asks how they can expect God to withhold judgment.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon contrasts the people's present condition with their having been civil and delightsome only a few years earlier.
Mormon asks how they can expect God to stay his hand in judgment and cries out in woe for the people.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown in a solitary moment of grief while writing.
unspecified_visual_details: No visible appearance of God or judgment is described.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The plea for judgment is prayerful speech, not a narrated divine action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict God appearing or judgment occurring.

title: Widows left to wander
summary: Mormon reports that widows and their daughters remain in Sherrizah after the Lamanites and Zenephi's army carried away provisions, leaving them to wander for food; many old women faint and die along the way.

explicit_facts.text: Many widows and their daughters remain in Sherrizah; the Lamanites and Zenephi's army carried away provisions, leaving them to wander for food.
Many old women faint and die by the way.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The account can be conveyed through a non-graphic image of the letter rather than depicting death.
unspecified_visual_details: The route, the number of survivors, and their appearance are unspecified.

narration.text: many old women do faint by the way and die

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a reported condition, not necessarily an event witnessed by Mormon in the moment of writing.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show graphic death or invent a specific journey location.

title: Mormon's army is weak
summary: Mormon reports that his army is weak, the Lamanite armies lie between him and Sherrizah, and those who fled to Aaron's army became victims of brutality. He says he can no longer enforce his commands.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says his army is weak and the Lamanite armies are between it and him.
Mormon reports that people who fled to Aaron's army fell victim to brutality.
Mormon says he cannot any longer enforce his commands.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing about his loss of authority.
unspecified_visual_details: The army's location, appearance, and the specific acts of brutality are not described.

narration.text: I cannot any longer enforce my commands

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The passage reports circumstances and does not stage a specific assault.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible battle, assault, or confrontation.

title: Suffering beyond words
summary: Mormon describes his people as brutal and without mercy, says suffering among women and children exceeds all telling, and declines to dwell further on the horrible scene.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says his people spare neither old nor young and take delight in everything save what is good.
Mormon says the suffering of women and children across the land exceeds what can be spoken or written, and that he will dwell no longer on it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown pausing over the letter as he refuses to elaborate.
unspecified_visual_details: No specific victims, acts, or setting are identified.

narration.text: tongue cannot tell, neither can it be written

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse explicitly withholds further detail; avoid illustrating unspecified atrocities.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent or visualize particular acts of violence.

title: Mormon recommends his son to God
summary: Mormon says he cannot recommend his people to God, but recommends his son and prays that he may live to witness the people's return or destruction, saying they must perish unless they repent and return.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says he cannot recommend his people to God lest God smite him.
Mormon recommends his son to God and prays that he may live to witness the people's return to God or their destruction.
Mormon says the people must perish unless they repent and return to God.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown writing a prayerful appeal to his son.
unspecified_visual_details: No divine appearance or response is described.
doctrinal_or_story_notes: The destruction is conditional and presented as Mormon's warning, not an event occurring here.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a divine smiting or the people's destruction.

title: Warning and request concerning the records
summary: Mormon warns that if the people perish, it will be like the Jaredites because of their bloodlust and revenge. He reports desertions to the Lamanites and asks his son to write if he is spared and Mormon perishes, while hoping to see him and deliver the sacred records.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon says the people's possible destruction would be like that of the Jaredites because of their willful hearts and desire for blood and revenge.
Mormon says many have deserted to the Lamanites and more will do so.
Mormon asks his son to write if spared and Mormon perishes; he hopes to see him soon and deliver sacred records.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The records may be represented as an object only if their appearance is kept generic; the verse does not describe them.
unspecified_visual_details: The Jaredites' historical destruction, the deserters, and any future meeting or delivery are not shown as current events.

narration.text: I have sacred records that I would deliver up unto thee

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The references to the Jaredites and future possibilities are reported or conditional, not present-time scenes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the Jaredites, desertions, a future reunion, or record delivery as occurring now.

title: Final blessing
summary: Mormon urges his son to be faithful in Christ and not be weighed down by the letter, praying that Christ and God's grace abide with him.

explicit_facts.text: Mormon urges his son to be faithful in Christ and prays that Christ lift him up rather than let the letter weigh him down.
Mormon prays that God's grace and the Lord Jesus Christ abide with his son forever.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Mormon may be shown concluding the letter.
unspecified_visual_details: The son is not stated to be present; no visible appearance of Christ or God is described.

narration.text: My son, be faithful in Christ

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Christ's suffering, death, and showing his body to the fathers are referenced in the letter, not depicted as events in this scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict Christ, God, a heavenly throne, or a past appearance as a present visual event.
